record.original_question: Does there exist a measure-preserving automorphism T of a probability space (X, B, mu) that is mixing but fails to be mixing of some higher order? Here T is k-fold mixing if for every measurable sets A, A_1, ..., A_k and every m_1, ..., m_k -> +infinity one has mu(A intersect T^{m_1}A_1 intersect T^{m_1+m_2}A_2 intersect ... intersect T^{m_1+...+m_k}A_k) -> mu(A)mu(A_1)...mu(A_k), and the paper denotes the class of such automorphisms by Mix(k).

evidence.quote: Автоморфизм T вероятностного пространства (X, B, µ) обладает свойством k-кратного перемешивания, если для всяких измеримых множеств A, A1, . . . , Ak при m1, . . . mk → +∞ выполняется µ(A ∩ T^{m1}A1 ∩ T^{m1+m2}A2 ∩ · · · ∩ T^{m1+···+mk} Ak) → µ(A)µ(A1). . . µ(Ak). Обозначим это свойство и класс соответствующих автоморфизмов через M ix(k).
Проблема Рохлина о кратном перемешивании. О непустоте классов M ix(k) \ M ix(k + 1) мы ничего не знаем.
Q1. Существует ли перемешивающий автоморфизм, не обладающий перемешиванием некоторой кратности?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $(X,\mathcal{B},\mu)$ be a standard probability space and let $T:X\to X$ be an invertible measure-preserving transformation. For an integer $k\ge 1$, say that $T$ is $k$-fold mixing (and write $T\in \mathrm{Mix}(k)$) if for every measurable sets $A,A_1,\dots,A_k\in\mathcal{B}$,
$$\mu\bigl(A\cap T^{m_1}A_1\cap T^{m_1+m_2}A_2\cap\cdots\cap T^{m_1+\cdots+m_k}A_k\bigr)\longrightarrow \mu(A)\,\mu(A_1)\cdots\mu(A_k)$$
as $m_1,\dots,m_k\to+\infty$ independently. Note that $\mathrm{Mix}(1)$ is the usual notion of mixing and $\mathrm{Mix}(k+1)\subseteq \mathrm{Mix}(k)$.

Question: Does there exist an invertible measure-preserving transformation $T$ of some probability space that is mixing (i.e. $T\in\mathrm{Mix}(1)$) but fails to be $k$-fold mixing for some $k\ge 2$? Equivalently, is the class $\mathrm{Mix}(k)\setminus\mathrm{Mix}(k+1)$ nonempty for some $k\ge 1$?
artifact.status_search_result: This is Rokhlin's classical problem on multiple mixing, posed in 1949 and widely regarded as still open. It is known that for transformations of finite rank (Kalikow) and more generally for finite-rank or rigid-type classes, mixing implies mixing of all orders, and Host proved that mixing implies mixing of all orders for transformations with singular spectrum. However, no example of a mixing transformation that fails to be higher-order mixing is known, and the general problem remains unresolved.

status_evidence.title: Rokhlin's multiple mixing problem (overview)
status_evidence.snippet: It is a long-standing open problem (Rokhlin's problem) whether every mixing transformation is mixing of all orders.
status_evidence.claim: The problem of whether mixing implies multiple mixing remains open in general.

status_evidence.title: Host, Mixing of all orders and pairwise independent joinings of systems with singular spectrum
status_evidence.snippet: Host (1991) proved mixing systems with singular spectrum are mixing of all orders.
status_evidence.claim: Partial results are known (Kalikow for rank one, Host for singular spectrum), but the general case is open.
